function: A worked stone set into the ground and kept. It does nothing a road can use and holds nobody; it exists so that something else can happen where it stands. Whoever raised it would rather see it broken than taken.
height_class: [needs decision: height class for building.ritual_anchor -- brief section 20, exact standard building dimensions]

tier_states.notes: Cut, set and left. Nothing about it is a building in the ordinary sense; it is on this list because it occupies ground and can be knocked down.

dungeon_relationship: Provisional: an anchor may be the reason a dungeon exists under it, which is C5's tomb question and S9's signature. Not decided here.
loot_relationship: Provisional: nothing portable. S10 owns loot tables.

notes: The second half of the capture decision, chosen deliberately the other way: destroy_only with clears_completely. An anchor cannot change hands -- taking it would mean the taker inherits what it anchors, and nothing in the design says that -- and breaking one is meant to free the ground rather than deny it. Both fields are this record's choice; brief section 20 leaves the rule Open per building type and S3's validate refuses a record that leaves either to the code.
One authored tier. Proves that a record may stop below TIER_CAP and that a production rule sitting at the record's own top tier is legal.
No entrance and no road socket: brief section 8 lists the socket kinds a building may declare, not the kinds it must. This record is the case that proves an empty socket field loads.
Open (brief section 20, exact resource list): construction_cost and output_key carry the placeholder resource.open.needs_decision.
Open: the site requirement flag and the service key are *.open.needs_decision.* placeholders; S13 and S9 own what satisfies and reads them.

Open (brief section 20, exact standard building dimensions): height_class is a needs-decision placeholder; maximum_slope is 0; the envelope is a share of CELL_CAPACITY_CELLS. Clearance is twice the footprint because what the brief counts as essential around this thing is the ground nobody else builds on.

No doctrine is authored here. faction_compatibility names concept keys only; the two concepts listed are the ones the brief already accepts, and nothing in this file says what either faction believes.
